ASHWIND LOG — Torvig Harbour, one week
(Invented material. In a subfolder on purpose: a folder source is walked
recursively, so this file has to turn up in knowledge/ as well.)

Day 1   NE 4    clear
Day 2   NE 5    clear, gusting 6 in the gap
Day 3   NE 6    spray over the pier at high water
Day 4   NE 3    fog over the Kestrel Deep from 06:00
Day 5   E 2     fog all day, mail boat cancelled
Day 6   NE 4    clear
Day 7   NE 5    clear

The ashwind blows on about 200 days a year. It is dry, it comes from the
north-east, and it is the reason the Ashwind Sea has its name. Fog is the
exception and occurs when warm air from the south meets the cold water over
the Kestrel Deep — as on days 4 and 5.
